Comparisons

Vibresia, compared

Each page here compares two apps: what each costs, what each is good at, and who should pick which. Most put Vibresia next to one other app; the rest are referee pages between two other apps. We make Vibresia, so every page also says when the other app is the better choice, and every fact about another app comes from its own site.

Vibresia is a free Mac app that turns whatever the Mac is playing into visuals. If you'd rather see every option for the Mac in one list, read the best music visualizers for Mac.

Vibresia vs Magic Music Visuals

Free to try; paid plans on its site · Mac, Windows

Magic Music Visuals is a modular editor for live visuals. If you only want visuals for what your Mac is playing, Vibresia is free and plays out of the box.

Vibresia vs Plane9

Free · Windows

Plane9 is a free 3D visualiser for Windows only. On a Mac, Vibresia is the free alternative that reacts to whatever is playing. Here's how they compare.

Vibresia vs projectM

Open source (LGPL) · Windows, Mac, Linux

projectM's Mac apps are still previews. Vibresia is a free, signed Mac visualiser that hears any app. Here's how they compare, and when projectM wins.

Vibresia vs Shadertoy

Not confirmed · Browser

Want your shaders to react to the music your Mac is playing? Vibresia is a free Mac app built for that. Shadertoy is better for everything else.

Vibresia vs Synesthesia

US$199, one-time · Mac, Windows

Want Synesthesia's visuals at home without paying US$199? Vibresia is a free Mac visualiser for whatever is playing. Here's where each one wins.

Vibresia vs TouchDesigner

Free version; paid from US$300 · Windows, Mac

If you only want visuals that move to music, TouchDesigner makes you build them. Vibresia is a free Mac visualiser that plays out of the box.

Questions people ask

Which comparison should I read?

Start with the app you use now, or the one you were about to try. If you'd rather see every option for the Mac in one list, read the best music visualizers for Mac.

Are these comparisons fair if you make Vibresia?

We have a reason to favour Vibresia, so every page says who the other app is better for, and every fact about the other app comes from a named source with the date it was checked.

Is Vibresia free?

Yes. Every feature is free, with no account and no trial, and the code is open source under the MIT licence. It needs macOS 14.2 or later on Apple silicon.
